Rashi on Nedarim 24b:1:1.hebrew: אפי' בקמייתא - הנך דלעיל, ש"מ:
Rashi on Nedarim 24b:1:1.english: Even in the earlier [cases] - Those [mentioned] above; conclude from it.

Rashi on Nedarim 24b:2:1.hebrew: מאי הוי עלה - אי הוי הלכתא כוותיה דר' אליעזר, דהוי נדרי זרוזין ומותר:
Rashi on Nedarim 24b:2:1.english: What was [concluded] about it - Whether the halakha is in accordance with Rabbi Eliezer, that they are vows of incitement and [it is] permitted.

Rashi on Nedarim 24b:6:1.hebrew: אמר ליה רבא - א"כ, מתניתא דאמר ״שבועה שראיתי בדרך הזה״:
Rashi on Nedarim 24b:6:1.english: Rava said to him - If so, [that] the Mishnah [refers to a case] where he said, "An oath that I saw on this road."

Rashi on Nedarim 24b:6:2.hebrew: למה לי למימר - דאסור, דהיינו שבועה גמורה ודאי, כאילו אמר שבועה שאכלתי:
Rashi on Nedarim 24b:6:2.english: Why do I [need] to say [it] - that it is forbidden? For that is certainly a full-fledged oath, as if he had said, "An oath that I ate."

Rashi on Nedarim 24b:6:3.hebrew: ועודי דומיא דנדר קתני - שבועות (נדרי) הבאי אסורין, דמשמע דקאמר בלשון נדר ושבועה:
Rashi on Nedarim 24b:6:3.english: And furthermore, it teaches [that it is] similar to a vow - "Oaths (vows) of exaggeration are forbidden," which implies that he speaks using the language of [both] a vow and an oath.

Rashi on Nedarim 24b:6:4.hebrew: אלא אמר רבא - קאמר הכי, "יאסרו כל פירות העולם עלי בשבועה":
Rashi on Nedarim 24b:6:4.english: Rather, Rava said - [He] says thus: "All the produce of the world shall be forbidden to me by an oath."

Rashi on Nedarim 24b:6:5.english: If I did not see - And he does not say "that I saw."

Rashi on Nedarim 24b:7:1.hebrew: אמר ליה רבינא - אמאי אסורות? ודלמא שפיר אישתבע לדעתיה דידיה:
Rashi on Nedarim 24b:7:1.english: Ravina said to him - Why are [the fruits] forbidden? And perhaps he swore properly according to his own intention.

Rashi on Nedarim 24b:7:2.hebrew: דלמא קינא דשומשמני - נמלות מקובצות הרבה ראה ביחד כעולי מצרים, דאפשר:
Rashi on Nedarim 24b:7:2.english: Perhaps a nest of ants - He saw many ants gathered together, like those who ascended from Egypt, for [it is] possible.

Tosafot on Nedarim 24b:2:1.hebrew: מאי הויא עלה - וא"ת: והא פשיטנא כבר דפליגי רבנן עליה? לכן נראה לפרש: הלכה כרבי אליעזר ב"י או לא:
Tosafot on Nedarim 24b:2:1.english: "What was [concluded] about this matter?" - And if you ask: But we already resolved that the Rabbis disagree with him! Therefore, it appears [necessary] to explain [that the Gemara's question means]: Is the halakha in accordance with Rabbi Eliezer ben Ya'akov or not?

Tosafot on Nedarim 24b:3:1.hebrew: נדרי הבאי אם לא ראיתי - פירוש: שאמר קונם פירות העולם עלי אם לא ראיתי וכו' — מותרין, מטעם דעבידי אינשי דמשתעי הכי כדי לאמת ולצדק את דבריהן כשרואין מעשה אחד יותר ממה שרגיל להיות, ואין בלבו לאסור, ואנן סהדי, כדפרישית לעיל:
Tosafot on Nedarim 24b:3:1.english: "Vows of exaggeration ... if I did not see" - Explanation: [This means] that he said, "Konam [be] the produce of the world to me if I did not see, etc." — they are permitted, for the reason that people tend to speak this way in order to validate and substantiate their words when they see something greater than what is usual, and he has no [intention] in his heart to forbid [anything], and we are witnesses [to this], as I explained above.

Tosafot on Nedarim 24b:3:2.english: As those who ascended [from] Egypt - Because he saw a large multitude, more than [is] usual.

Tosafot on Nedarim 24b:3:3.hebrew: נחש טרוף - לפי שראוהו טרוף — יותר משאר נחשים. ודווקא כשראה כדפרישית, אבל אם לא ראה שום אדם ולא שום נחש, ודאי לא הוי נדר הבאי ואסור, דלא אמרינן משום דעבידי אינשי דמישתעו הכי, כיון שלא ראה כלל:
Tosafot on Nedarim 24b:3:3.english: A fierce snake - Because they saw it [as] fierce — more [so] than other snakes. And this is specifically when he saw [something], as I explained [above]; however, if he did not see any person or any snake, it is certainly not a vow of exaggeration and is forbidden, [for we do not say it is permitted] because people are accustomed to speak like this, since he did not see [anything] at all.

Tosafot on Nedarim 24b:6:1.english: Rather, Rava said, where he says, "All the produce in the world shall be forbidden, etc." - [In Shevuot, Tosafot explained this at length.]
